input: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

business.claim: People Center, Inc., popularly known as Rippling, is a Delaware corporation headquartered in San Francisco.

Company claim; observed as_of 2026-11-10: sells businesses a unified platform spanning HR, payroll, benefits, recruiting, identity and device management, corporate spending, and AI-powered administration.

Company claim; observed as_of 2026-11-10: customers purchase a required core platform plus selected modules. Most products use per-employee, per-month subscription pricing; some include a monthly base fee. Pricing is customized.

Company claim; observed as_of 2026-11-10: operates internationally, with offices in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, India, Australia, and Singapore. Office locations do not establish product availability in every jurisdiction.

traction.claim: Company claim; observed as_of 2026-11-10: customer-stories page states more than 30,000 customers and names NinjaTech AI and Kleiner Perkins. Customer count and relationships were not independently confirmed.

Company claim; observed as_of 2026-11-10: NinjaTech AI uses Rippling AI for workforce reporting across its international operations; its case study describes generating and checking an investor-ready report in roughly 100 seconds.
Company claim; as_of 2026-05-05: its accountant and HR-advisor partner program included advisory-board participation from theFinanceStack, Countsy, Ignite Spot, and Praxi Management.

Company claim, accessed through a third-party X mirror: on 2026-11-06, CEO Parker Conrad reported more than $150 million of net-new annual recurring revenue in Q3 2026, attributing a substantial contribution to Rippling AI. This is not quarterly recognized revenue.

team.claim: Forbes reports that Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar cofounded Rippling in 2016. Conrad previously founded Zenefits; Sankar was its director of engineering and served as Rippling CTO until 2020.

Company leadership page, observed as_of 2026-11-10: Parker Conrad is cofounder and CEO; Matt MacInnis is president and CPO; Matt Plank is CRO; Albert Strasheim is CTO; Adam Swiecicki is CFO; Martin White is general counsel; Bridget Abraham is chief compliance officer.
Company leadership page, observed as_of 2026-11-10: Stephanie Ho leads customer experience, and Sunil Raman leads business and product operations.
Company biography, observed as_of 2026-11-10: Matt MacInnis previously cofounded and led Inkling and worked at Apple.

Company claim; post observed as_of 2026-11-10: Sonia Parandekar joined as SVP and India site lead, following roles at Microsoft, Groupon, Urban Ladder, and Atlassian. The opened post did not expose an exact announcement date.

Aggregator data, last updated as_of 2025-12-16: SignalHire lists former CPO Eisar Lipkovitz's Rippling tenure as January 2024–January 2025 and employment at Netflix beginning September 2025. This departure falls within the review window but requires employer confirmation.

Bloomberg Law reported that Chris Handman replaced Vanessa Wu as general counsel in May 2025; Wu transitioned to senior counsel and remained with Rippling. This was a role change, not a reported company departure; Handman is not the general counsel shown on the currently opened leadership page.

Company claim; as_of 2026-11-06: the Reprompt AI team, including founders Lukas Martinelli and Rob Balian, joined Rippling to develop AI agents. Martinelli previously held an executive role at Mapbox; Balian previously worked at Robinhood and Facebook.

funding.claim: As_of 2023-03-17: investor counsel Gunderson Dettmer confirmed a $500 million financing led by Greenoaks.

As_of 2024-04-22: investor counsel confirmed a $200 million Series F led by Coatue, with Greenoaks participating, at a $13.5 billion valuation. The combined financing and common-stock transaction was described as up to approximately $790 million, not all primary capital.

Company claim; as_of 2025-05-09: raised $450 million in Series G financing at a $16.8 billion valuation and signed agreements for up to $200 million of employee and former-employee share repurchases. Investors included Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford, Y Combinator, and existing investors.

Research-provider data, observed as_of 2026-11-10: Sacra says the May 2025 Series G had no lead investor and continues to identify its $16.8 billion valuation. That is the last priced-round valuation verified here, not a current executable share price.

financial_signals.claim: Sacra estimate: annualized revenue reached $1 billion as_of March 2026, versus $850 million as_of year-end 2025, with 78% year-over-year growth reported for March 2026. These are third-party estimates, not audited annual recognized revenue.
Company claim; undated post observed as_of 2026-11-10: Rippling reported nearly 7,000 employees when introducing Helpdesk. A consistently dated headcount series was not verified.
Observed as_of 2026-11-10: Rippling maintains an active careers page directing candidates to open roles. A validated vacancy count and company-wide layoff history were not established.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In People Center v. Deel, the federal court allowed Rippling's racketeering and federal trade-secret claims to proceed while dismissing its state-law claims as preempted. The ruling addressed pleading sufficiency, not whether espionage occurred or customer data was breached.

The federal court compelled arbitration of counterclaims concerning a Rippling employee's alleged access to Deel's platform, stayed related data-access and RICO counterclaims, and allowed portions of Deel's false-advertising counterclaim to continue. It denied Deel's request to strike Keith O'Brien's affidavit; these were not final liability findings.

Aggregator/AI-generated legal summary: Court, Explained reports a discovery order dated 2026-11-07 requiring specified Rippling–O'Brien counsel communications and privilege logs by 2026-11-16. The underlying order was not accessible for independent verification.

Sanctions-related allegations, not regulator findings: Deel's amended complaint alleges that Rippling initiated Russia-related payments subsequently blocked by its payment processor. The complaint also records Rippling's denial that it transmitted payments to sanctioned countries, entities, individuals, or banks.
Bloomberg Law reported that Runlayer dropped its trade-secret suit against Rippling and Rippling's responsive patent suit also ended.

A file-stamped Orange County complaint names People Center d/b/a Rippling as defendant in David Behar's parental-leave interference, retaliation, and wrongful-termination action. These are plaintiff allegations; the opened complaint does not establish liability or current disposition.

reputation.claim: Employee-review aggregator snapshot as_of 2026-11-10: Glassdoor showed 3.6/5 overall from 1,313 reviews, 66% recommending the employer, and 3.0/5 for work-life balance. Recent visible reviews mixed positive culture and growth comments with demanding-workload concerns; a historical ratings trend was not verified.

Customer-review aggregator snapshot as_of 2026-11-10: Trustpilot displayed 4.6/5 from 2,779 reviews. Its AI-generated summary emphasized usability while noting glitches and implementation difficulties. The profile disclosed a paid subscription and customer review invitations.

BBB review snapshot as_of 2026-11-10: customer rating was 1.41/5 from 29 reviews, alongside an A+ BBB business rating. Visible complaints repeatedly concerned support escalation, onboarding, payroll reliability, and refunds or contracts. These are self-selected customer allegations, not findings or a measured incident rate.

red_flags.claim: Diligence inference: competitor litigation creates continuing exposure and management-distraction risk. Some false-advertising allegations against Rippling survived dismissal, while other counterclaims were stayed rather than resolved on their merits.

Diligence inference: independently test payment-screening controls and investigate the disputed Russia-related transactions. The cited allegations and Rippling's denial do not establish a sanctions violation.

Diligence inference: recurring support, implementation, and payroll complaints warrant administrator-level reference calls and incident-history review; the small, self-selected BBB sample cannot establish prevalence.
Diligence inference: weaker work-life-balance ratings warrant checking regretted attrition, management practices, and retention by function rather than relying on the overall employee rating.

Diligence inference: the revenue estimate is annualized rather than audited recognized revenue. Reconcile it to reported ARR, revenue recognition, retention, gross margin, and cash consumption before underwriting valuation.

output.verdict: As_of 2026-11-10, Rippling's broad platform, named customer references, substantial financing, and reported growth support further diligence. The main underwriting gaps are verified revenue quality and cash economics, administrator-level service reliability, payment controls, and unresolved competitor litigation; growth claims and procedural court victories should not substitute for audited financials or final findings.

cost_basis: tokens x list price + $10 per 1K web search calls
